note: Mind's-eye coherence test for lyrics. A blind reader (fresh Claude agent; it sees only the lyric, under a neutral filename) says what it pictures. The bar is BlazeDale's (2026-10-17): a listener should be able to piece together a picture that means something to them. It does not have to be the author's intent. one_word records the reader's single-word change suggestion plus Claude's consideration of it. Suggestions are tracked, not applied, unless BlazeDale says so.

readers.v1: PICTURE (2-4 sentences) / VERDICT: ADDS UP or FRAGMENTS / LOOSE LINES. Result: 14 of 14 ADDS UP. Five copies on one lyric (Static) gave near-identical pictures, all hedged with 'maybe a radio, maybe a dead line'. Too charitable to separate songs.
readers.v2: Commit to ONE concrete picture, no hedging / FROM THE LYRIC / INVENTED / MEANING / VERDICT: ADDS UP, THIN or FRAGMENTS / LOOSE LINES / ONE WORD. Result: 15 of 15 ADDS UP, no THIN. The verdict still doesn't separate songs, but INVENTED does: Static's whole visible scene was invented. ONE WORD produced specific, often good fixes.
readers.v3: Mark every sung line, repeats included: P (something to see), F (feeling only) or X (does not fit). Then PICTURE / INVENTED / ONE WORD. Result: the first reader that separates songs. Picture share runs from 0% (Static) to 67% (caravan). The image-lab songs written before the rule score lowest (0, 9, 23%); pilot songs score 24-67%. P% measures concreteness, not quality: check it against BlazeDale's hearts before treating it as a gate.

findings: Repeat suggestions: separate readers in separate runs proposed the IDENTICAL one-word change on 4 songs (963 burning->rowing, 988 hour->ocean, 1010 home->here, 1009 floor->ice). On 997 they agreed on the same target word (love) but not the replacement. A change two blind readers both ask for is the strongest signal this test makes.
Choruses carry the feeling and verses carry the picture: in 1000, all 12 P lines sit in the verses and builds, and both choruses are pure F.
A reader always builds a picture. The signal is how much of that picture it had to invent (Static: everything; the gate song: almost nothing).
Taste check: the first hearted lyric scored 9% picture (Wish It Anyway). Don't gate on P%.

Brief lesson (954): an abstract heroic shape (a long stair to a light, a voice above) produced motivational-poster lyrics on two rolls ('hold on', 'only way out is through'). Re-grounding the SAME shape in ordinary life (a box up a stairwell on moving day, a friend counting floors down) gave the second voice a real job, and the reader recovered the scene exactly.

hearts.note: BlazeDale hearted it. It scored 9% on v3, among the lowest. First evidence that P% is not taste: a mostly-feeling lyric can land.
